Hi Liam — thanks for the heads up and for sending the uptime log. We saw the same degraded window in our serving telemetry (impacted three routes). I will loop in Marissa (CS ops) and Sean (finance) to walk through eligibility and next steps.

Quick answers:
- We can calculate eligibility on our side using the combined telemetry; if you want to submit your own metric pack we can cross-check.
- Typical turnaround for a first-pass eligibility check is 3 business days; formal credit issuance (if approved) can take up to 10 business days after approval due to finance processing.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa will evaluate uptime & impact;
2) Sean will confirm payout mechanics and provide estimate;
3) I'll follow up with a one-page mutual action plan for sign-off.

Hi all — I pulled the incident digest from our ops playbook and attached a short postmortem. Preliminary notes: the outage window started at 09:02 UTC and ended at 09:47 UTC; two autoscale helpers failed to warm which increased queueing and raised tail latency. Total route-level unavailability (per contract definition) = 40 minutes across affected routes; SLA definition uses rolling 30-day uptime so we still need to calculate whether that translates to a credit slab.

I've attached: postmortem-digest-20260614.pdf and the raw telemetry slice. Can you confirm whether Avalon wants Redwood to draft the credit calculation or if you prefer to provide a reconciliation sheet?

Marissa
